newsitem.title: UK: BT asks for removal of takeover rule - paper.
newsitem.headline: BT asks for removal of takeover rule - paper.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc has asked the UK government to remove its protection against takeovers provided since the privatisation in 1984 by the so- called "golden share" in the company, said the Independent newspaper.

The move is aimed at persuading U.S. regulators to approve BT's planned 13 billion stg takeover of MCI Communications, America's long distance telephone operator, by showing that Britain is open to competition and BT is no longer protected from takeover, said the paper.
The golden share allows the government to veto changes to BT's constitution, which prevents anyone from owning more than 15 percent of the shares.
The provisions, which also apply to Cable and Wireless, privatised in 1981, were designed to prevent the companies from being bought by hostile overseas predators.
